title: How Long Is the Warranty on a New HVAC System?
h1: How Long Is the Warranty on a New HVAC System?
description: Most new HVAC equipment carries a manufacturer parts warranty that gets longer if you register it. Labor is separate. Here's how the coverage works.
quick_answer: Most major brands give new residential HVAC equipment a limited parts warranty, commonly around five years, that often extends to ten years when you register the equipment within the required window. Some parts, like a furnace heat exchanger, may carry longer coverage. Labor is usually not included in the manufacturer warranty and depends on your installer.
body:
What does an HVAC warranty actually cover?

A new system usually comes with two separate kinds of coverage, and people often mix them up.

  • Manufacturer parts warranty: covers the cost of replacement parts that fail because of a defect, such as a compressor, control board, motor or coil. It's set by the equipment brand and printed in the warranty document for your model.
  • Labor warranty: covers the cost of the technician's time to diagnose and replace those parts. This comes from the contractor who installed the system, not the manufacturer, and terms vary from company to company.

So even when a part is covered, you could still owe for labor, refrigerant or other materials unless your installer's labor coverage includes them. Ask about both before you sign.

Why does registration matter so much?

With many brands, the longer parts warranty only kicks in if the equipment is registered online within a set window after installation, often 60 or 90 days. Miss the window and coverage may drop to the shorter base term.

Some installers register equipment for you. Others leave it to the homeowner. Either way, check that it's done and keep the confirmation. You'll want the model and serial numbers of the indoor and outdoor units, the install date and the installer's name.

How long do the different parts tend to be covered?

Every brand and model line is different, so the warranty document for your exact equipment is the final word. In general:

  • Most components such as motors, boards and valves fall under the standard parts warranty.
  • Compressors on some higher-end air conditioners and heat pumps carry longer coverage than the rest of the unit.
  • Furnace heat exchangers often have a longer warranty than the rest of the furnace, sometimes much longer.
  • Accessories like thermostats, air cleaners and UV lights usually have their own separate terms.

What can void an HVAC warranty?

Manufacturer warranties come with conditions. Common reasons a claim gets denied include:

  • The system wasn't registered on time, so only the base coverage applies.
  • The equipment was installed by someone not qualified to do it, or not to the manufacturer's instructions.
  • There's no record of regular maintenance, if the warranty requires it.
  • A repair used parts the manufacturer doesn't allow, or the wrong refrigerant.
  • Damage came from outside causes like flooding, power surges, rodents or physical impact.
  • The home was sold and the warranty wasn't transferable, or the transfer steps weren't followed.

Keep a simple folder with the install invoice, registration confirmation and every service receipt. It makes a claim much easier if you ever need one.

What should you do when something breaks under warranty?

  1. Call the company that installed the system first. They handle most warranty diagnostics and can tell you what's covered.
  2. Have your model and serial numbers, install date and registration confirmation ready.
  3. Ask up front which costs are covered by the parts warranty, which by the installer's labor coverage, and which you'd pay.
  4. Keep copies of the repair invoice showing the failed part and what was replaced.

Are extended warranties worth it?

Some manufacturers and contractors offer extended parts and labor plans for an added cost. Whether one makes sense depends on how long you plan to stay in the home, the equipment you chose and what the plan actually covers.

Read the fine print for deductibles, exclusions and who does the repairs. A plan that requires yearly maintenance is only useful if you'll actually schedule it.

What about homes near the coast?

Salt air can corrode outdoor coils and cabinets on homes close to the ocean. Some manufacturers treat corrosion damage differently, so if you live near the beach, ask about coil coatings and read how the warranty handles corrosion. Rinsing the outdoor unit and keeping up with tune-ups helps either way.

When you're comparing new systems, our HVAC team can walk you through the manufacturer warranty on each option and explain what labor coverage comes with the install, as part of a free estimate.
faqs: Is labor included in an HVAC manufacturer warranty?
Usually not. The manufacturer warranty typically covers replacement parts only. Labor coverage comes from your installing contractor and varies, so ask for it in writing.
Does an HVAC warranty transfer to a new owner?
Some do and some don't. Certain brands allow a transfer with registration and a fee within a set time after the sale. Check the warranty document for your specific equipment.
Do I have to get yearly maintenance to keep my warranty?
Many manufacturers require proper maintenance and can deny claims for failures caused by neglect. Keeping service receipts is the easiest way to show the system has been cared for.
How do I find my HVAC warranty?
Look on the manufacturer's website using the model and serial numbers from the unit labels. Your installer's invoice and any registration email should also list the coverage.
